content: The dispute involved ex-spouses disagreeing over the physical divisibility of their former family home. The court examined the concept of "convenient divisibility" (comoda divisibilità) under Articles 720 and 1116 of the Civil Code,. The interpretive problem was defining when a property is legally indivisible due to technical or economic burdens,. The court concluded that because the proposed split would require highly expensive renovations, create invasive easements (such as access to shared attics through one unit), and cause a significant depreciation in value, the house was not conveniently divisible and must be sold at auction.
